title: Local Spin Excitations Mediate Quasiparticle Breakdown in the Orbital-Selective Mott Phase
authors: Yuekun Niu, Yu Ni, Jia-Ming Wang, Zhong-Yi Lu, Yun Song, Shiping Feng
abstract: The orbital-selective Mott phase (OSMP) is commonly described as a coexistence of localized and itinerant electrons within effectively decoupled orbitals, but emerging evidence for quasiparticle breakdown points to physics beyond this picture, whose microscopic origin remains unknown. Using dynamical mean-field theory for the two-band Hubbard model, we show that the spin-flip and Ising-type components of Hund's coupling generate local spin excitations (LSEs). These LSEs couple electrons between different orbitals, renormalize quasiparticle lifetimes and binding energies, and thereby destroy well-defined quasiparticles in the OSMP. Removing these two components of Hund's coupling restores coherent quasiparticle behavior and fully decouples the charge dynamics of the two bands. Our results therefore identify electronic coupling to LSEs as the fundamental mechanism driving quasiparticle breakdown within the OSMP.
summary: This theoretical work investigates why quasiparticles break down in the Orbital-Selective Mott Phase (OSMP) using DMFT on a two-band Hubbard model. The key finding is that this breakdown is driven by Local Spin Excitations (LSEs), which are generated by specific components of Hund's coupling. Removing these LSE pathways restores coherent, well-defined quasiparticle behavior.
main_problem: The study aims to uncover the microscopic mechanism responsible for quasiparticle breakdown observed in the Orbital-Selective Mott Phase (OSMP), moving beyond simple models of decoupled orbitals.
main_result: The authors identify that electronic coupling mediated by Local Spin Excitations (LSEs)—specifically those generated by the spin-flip and Ising components of Hund's coupling—is the fundamental mechanism driving this quasiparticle breakdown in the OSMP.
method: Dynamical Mean-Field Theory (DMFT) is employed to analyze the two-band Hubbard model, calculating spectral functions and correlation metrics across different interaction regimes.
model_or_system: The system is modeled using a two-band Hubbard Hamiltonian on a Bethe lattice. The interactions include Coulomb repulsion ($U$) and Hund's coupling terms ($J_{sf}, J_z$), which are varied to isolate their physical roles.
key_observables: Local Spin Excitations (LSE) spectral function ($	ext{ALSE}(\omega)$), Local Two-Qubit Fidelity (LTQF), and the orbital Density of States ($ho_\alpha(\omega)$).
important_parameters: The critical parameters are the interaction strengths ($U, J_{sf}, J_z$) and the system's filling level, particularly focusing on the OSMP regime.
main_assumptions: The analysis utilizes DMFT applied to an effective single-impurity model; some derivations rely on Hartree-Fock approximations for analytical insight.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the evolution of the LSE spectrum across different interaction strengths, showing a sharp weight transfer to the Fermi level only within the OSMP regime. LTQF values are used to diagnose deviations from ideal metallic or insulating states.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical problem (OSMP breakdown), develops theoretical tools (DMFT, LSE definition), calculates observables across varying Hund's coupling components, and concludes by linking the observed spectral weight transfer directly to LSE mediation.
why_interesting: The concept of LSE-mediated dynamic coupling provides a concrete, microscopic mechanism for correlated electron phenomena like quasiparticle breakdown, which is highly relevant to understanding strongly interacting quantum materials.
